CO2 is an essential volatile factor in the stimulation of hyphal development by the obligately biotroph symbiont Gigaspora margaria, and that this fungal symbiont can fix root exudate derived CO2.
the symbiosis between the fungus Gigaspora and carrot roots is stimulated by root volatiles, especially CO2, and that root exudates are also required for optimal growth.
CO2 and root exudate components are required for hyphal development and growth of the vesicular-arbuscular mycorrihzal fungus Gigasporamargarita.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of carbon dioxide in the development and maintenance of the mycorrhizas, and the possible role of carbon dioxide as a signal molecule in the symbiosis.
the mechanisms of the symbiotic interaction between the obligate biotroph, G. margarita, and its host, Daucus carota.
the role of root exudates and volatile factors on hyphal growth of Gigaspora margatita, and the importance of carbon dioxide in the establishment of vesicular arbuscualr mycorrhizae.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the symbiosis is stimulated by the interaction between root volatiles and root exudate, with carbon dioxide being the critical root volatile.
the symbiotic interaction between the host and the fungus is a mutualistic association.
the root exudates are a signal that the fungus can sense, and the CO2 is the signal that the fungus uses to grow.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CO2 and root exudation are two critical factors in fungal growth stimulation in vesicular arbusular mycorrhizas.
root volatiles, particularly CO2, and root exuded factors are both essential in the early stages of hyphal development of the obligately biotroph G. margarita.
the fungus is stimulated by a combination of CO2 and root exudate factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fungus has to be in the right place to get the right food.
the symbiotic interaction between plants and fungi is more than a simple exchange of carbon for phosphate.
the symbiosis is a dynamic and interactive process that requires the participation of both the host and fungal partners to establish a functional symbiosis.
